root_idea.summary: The root centers on forceful rebuke or a cry that drives, turns, or holds someone or something back.
root_idea.development: From vocal admonition and repulsion, the root extends to driving or urging onward, the cry or act by which this is done, deterrence, and specialized uses such as augury.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.
Displayed as the distinct Quran-attested nominal form.

Displayed under the normalized singular feminine active-participle citation form زَاجِرَة.

senses.definition: To be driven away or repelled.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passive construction, the subject is portrayed as driven away by a dismissive cry or similar act of expulsion.

senses.definition: A deterrent or means of driving away and preventing, especially from committing sinful acts.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use is also interpreted as prevention from punishment; the form is treated lexically as a noun of deterrence despite its QAC participial morphology.

senses.definition: A threat or warning intended to deter.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative interpretation of the Quranic construction in which the form denotes a warning held out against wrongdoing.

senses.definition: Driving or urging, especially by a forceful cry.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction at 37:2, it denotes the driving or urging associated with the preceding active participle, traditionally understood as the driving of clouds.
The Quranic occurrences describe a single resounding cry associated with the sudden occurrence of resurrection.

senses.definition: One who drives or urges; in the Quranic plural, a driver of the clouds.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic feminine plural is interpreted as the angels who drive the clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To chide, reprove, check, restrain, forbid, or prevent someone from an act, by rough speech, a voice, or a cry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction commonly takes عَنْ for the act or thing from which someone is restrained; it can also be directed at an animal by a cry to make it refrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive or urge an animal or other thing onward by a characteristic cry; of the wind, to drive clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes urging camels, sheep, horses, and beasts of prey, as well as the figurative expression of wind driving clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry or act of crying out, especially one used to chide, drive, or urge; by extension, the driving away effected by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the nominal expression for the cry or driving action and includes cries directed at animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To augur or divine from birds or other omens; divination based on their flight, landing, cries, kinds, or names.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage belongs to the traditional practice of interpreting auspicious or inauspicious signs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away or depart in the idiom زَجَرَ غُرَابَ البَيْنِ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic expression associated with the crow of separation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to cast forth what was in her belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied lexical evidence records this as a specialized usage of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mutually chide, restrain, prevent, or forbid one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction is used of mutual restraint from evil or reprehensible conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be chided, checked, restrained, or forbidden and consequently refrain or abstain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes عَنْ for the act from which one refrains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become urged or incited by a cry to pursue game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence illustrates the usage with an animal responding to a driving cry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of large fish with small scales.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This regional or attributed term is reported with doubt as to its genuineness in Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel with reluctant or abnormal nursing behavior, requiring chastisement to yield milk or rejecting or misdirecting acceptance of young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also reported metaphorically as an epithet for war, though the precise figurative nuance is not specified.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who chides, checks, restrains, or forbids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related intensive form زَجَّار denotes one who performs this frequently or to a marked degree. The expression كَفَى بِالقُرْآنِ زَاجِرًا applies the term to the Quran as a restraining or forbidding influence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exhorter or inward restraining influence that invites a believer toward the truth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence describes this as an influence in the heart rather than an external cry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A diviner or interpreter of omens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is connected with crying out against an undertaking judged to be inauspicious; أَبُو زَاجِر is also an epithet for the crow in this augury-related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chiding, restraining, or exhortatory speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine substantive occurs in the plural alongside مواعظ for repeated admonitions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel with looseness, sores, or a fracture affecting the vertebrae of its back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized anatomical or veterinary adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of chiding, driving away, or similar restraint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom هُوَ مِنِّي مَزْجَرَ الكَلْبِ portrays someone as being in a position where he may be chided and driven away like a dog.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or means of chiding, driving away, or preventing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote a deterrent cause, including remembrance of God as a means of driving away the devil.

cautions: For مُزْدَجَر, QAC marks the occurrence as a passive participle, while the lexical evidence also treats it as an infinitive noun and records alternative interpretations.
The lexical evidence reports an alternative reading مَزَّجَر for مُزْدَجَر; the public form follows the canonical QAC identification.
Historical Quran citation notation in the lexical evidence was not converted directly into modern verse locations; the displayed modern locations are the independently supplied QAC locations.
